q: Which component lets an administrator power-cycle a server and view its console even when the operating system has crashed?
explain: The BMC provides out-of-band hardware management independent of the OS.

q: Which modern standard provides a RESTful (JSON over HTTPS) API for server hardware management through the BMC?
explain: Redfish is the modern REST API; IPMI is the older protocol.

q: Which NVIDIA software provisions OS images to cluster nodes and manages cluster configuration and workload managers?
explain: Base Command Manager (formerly Bright Cluster Manager) handles provisioning and cluster management.

q: A common monitoring stack collects GPU metrics as time series and displays dashboards and alerts. Which pair is typically used?
explain: DCGM Exporter feeds Prometheus; Grafana visualizes.

q: A multi-node job fails only on certain nodes. Investigation shows different GPU driver versions across nodes. What is the best long-term fix?
options: Manage nodes from a single golden image and roll updates consistently with a cluster manager
Install drivers by hand on each node when jobs fail
explain: Configuration consistency prevents version drift.

q: Which tool is used to manage data center facilities such as power, cooling, space, and assets?
explain: DCIM covers facility-level monitoring and capacity planning.

q: A node reports a hardware GPU error. What should the operator do FIRST in the scheduler?
options: Drain the node so no new jobs start on it
Reboot all nodes in the cluster
explain: Draining isolates the node while running jobs finish; then diagnose.

q: Which management network should carry IPMI/Redfish traffic to server BMCs?
explain: BMC traffic stays on the OOB network, isolated from production traffic.

q: Which scheduler is traditionally used for large multi-node batch training and HPC jobs on GPU clusters?
explain: Slurm is the standard HPC workload manager.

q: In Kubernetes, which resource name does a pod request to get one full NVIDIA GPU?
explain: The NVIDIA device plugin advertises nvidia.com/gpu.

q: What does the NVIDIA GPU Operator do in a Kubernetes cluster?
options: It automates deployment of the GPU driver, container toolkit, device plugin, GPU feature discovery, DCGM exporter, and MIG manager
explain: The GPU Operator manages all software needed to use GPUs in Kubernetes.

q: Which Slurm command shows the state of partitions and nodes?
explain: sinfo shows partitions and node states; squeue shows jobs.

q: Which Slurm scheduling feature lets small jobs start earlier in idle gaps without delaying higher-priority jobs?
explain: Backfill fills scheduling gaps.

q: Which NVIDIA product adds team quotas, fair-share, and fractional GPU allocation on top of Kubernetes to raise GPU utilization?
explain: Run:ai is a Kubernetes-based GPU orchestration platform.

q: Which Slurm plugins let users run NGC container images as part of their jobs?
explain: Pyxis (SPANK plugin) + Enroot run containers in Slurm.

q: Which workload is a better fit for Kubernetes than for Slurm?
options: A tightly coupled MPI weather simulation
A large multi-node pre-training batch job
explain: Kubernetes is designed for services with deployments and autoscaling.

q: Which GPU Operator component labels nodes with GPU model, memory, and MIG capabilities?
explain: GPU Feature Discovery (GFD) generates node labels.

q: What is the main advantage of containers compared with virtual machines for AI workloads?
options: Containers include a full guest OS kernel
Containers are lightweight, share the host kernel, and package the application and its libraries consistently
explain: Containers are portable and lightweight.

q: Which NVIDIA tool provides GPU health checks, diagnostics, and telemetry at data center scale?
explain: DCGM manages and monitors GPUs in clusters.

q: A GPU shows 100% 'GPU utilization' in nvidia-smi, but training is slower than expected. Which metric gives a better view of how much of the GPU is actually busy?
explain: GPU utilization only measures the time a kernel runs; SM activity measures how many SMs are busy.

q: An H100 shows 88 °C temperature and SM clocks well below maximum under load. What is the most likely issue?
explain: High temperature plus reduced clocks indicates thermal throttling.

q: What does XID 79 in the kernel log indicate?
options: The GPU has fallen off the bus
explain: XID 79 is a serious hardware/PCIe event; drain, power-cycle, diagnose.

q: What is the difference between single-bit (SBE) and double-bit (DBE) ECC errors?
options: SBEs crash the application; DBEs are harmless
SBEs are corrected by ECC; DBEs are uncorrectable and can crash applications
explain: SBE = corrected (watch trend); DBE = uncorrectable (XID 48).

q: Which command runs an extended DCGM diagnostic on GPUs before returning a node to service?
explain: Run level 3 is the long diagnostic (level 1 quick, level 2 medium).

q: On which default port does NVIDIA DCGM Exporter publish Prometheus metrics?
explain: DCGM Exporter serves /metrics on port 9400.

q: GPU utilization is low while CPU usage is near 100% during training. What is the most likely bottleneck?
options: The data loading and preprocessing pipeline
explain: The GPUs wait for data; use more workers, DALI, or faster storage.

q: What is the maximum number of MIG GPU instances on an NVIDIA H100?
explain: MIG supports up to 7 instances on A100/H100/H200/B200.

q: Which GPU sharing method provides NO memory or fault isolation between workloads?
explain: Time-slicing shares the GPU by context switching without memory isolation.

q: Two different customers must share one H100 with guaranteed memory, cache, and compute. Which method fits best?
explain: MIG provides hardware-partitioned, isolated GPU instances.

q: What does the MIG profile name '3g.40gb' mean?
options: 3 compute slices and 40 GB of GPU memory
3 GB of memory and 40 compute units
explain: Format: <compute slices>g.<memory>gb.

q: Which requirements are specific to NVIDIA vGPU compared with MIG on bare metal?
options: A supported hypervisor and an NVIDIA software license
explain: vGPU runs in a hypervisor and needs licensing (e.g., through NVIDIA AI Enterprise for compute).

q: Which consideration argues AGAINST partitioning GPUs for a workload?
options: A large model training job that needs full GPUs and fast NVLink between them
explain: Large training needs whole GPUs and nodes; partitioning reduces available compute per job.

q: What must be done before creating MIG instances on a supported GPU?
options: Enable MIG mode on the GPU (nvidia-smi -mig 1), which requires a GPU reset
explain: MIG mode must be enabled first, then GPU and compute instances are created.
